# Develop-Only Film (No Scanning)

Not every roll of film needs scanning. When a customer orders developing only — for example choosing **"No thanks"** under your scanning option at the checkout — OrderHub can recognise this automatically, keep the roll out of your scanning queue, and finish the job the moment developing is done.

---

## How OrderHub knows a job is develop-only

You nominate which options on your film products mean "no scanning".

1. Go to **Settings** > **Organization** > **Film Development** > **Twin Checking**.
2. Find **"No scanning required" option mapping**.
3. Click **Add option key** and choose an option your storefront uses for the scanning question (for example `scanning-135` or `scanning-35mm`). Add a row for each key you use.
4. Under each key, tick the value or values that mean no scan (for example *No thanks*).
    * *Note: matching ignores capitals and spacing.*

![Develop Only Setting](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/54e62c0a-4617-402d-9291-4ebf2dd5b8a9.png)

From then on, new orders arriving with any of those choices are flagged develop-only from the start. This applies to **new orders only** — it never changes jobs that already exist.

---

## What your team sees

*   The roll carries a **Develop only** chip in the station app, so operators know not to expect scans.
*   It queues at **Develop** as normal but **never appears in the Scan queue**, and there is no "awaiting files" state — no files are ever coming.
*   Its due date is calculated **without your scanning hours** (see your Timings settings), so develop-only work is promised sooner.

---

## When is the job finished?

If **Auto-complete film jobs when all rolls are uploaded** is switched on (Settings > Organization > Film Development > General), it also covers develop-only work: when the last roll of a develop-only job is marked complete at Develop, **the job completes itself** — you'll see *"All rolls developed"* in the job's activity. The order then completes or stays open depending on its other jobs, exactly as normal. If the customer asked for their negatives back, hand them over as usual — that part stays physical.

If the auto-complete setting is off, develop-only jobs wait for you to complete them by hand.

---

## Overriding a single job

The **No scan needed** toggle on the order's Rolls tab still works for one-off cases in either direction — and a manual choice is always respected: the automatic mapping never overwrites something you set by hand.

---

## Good to know

*   Prints can't be ordered from unscanned film, and OrderHub enforces this naturally: automatic print jobs are only ever created when scans arrive, so a develop-only roll never creates prints.
*   Orders can mix: one scanned job and one develop-only job on the same order each follow their own path, and customer notifications stay correct for both.
